facts.raw_span: A 36‐year‐old man of Indian origin presented at 2:30 a.m. with acute right‐sided weakness and three episodes of vomiting
He awoke around midnight with headache and vomiting, then noted right‐sided numbness and weakness
no visual change or speech disturbance
pulse was 88 bpm
blood pressure 124/87 mmHg
oxygen saturation 98% on room air
Motor strength was 0/5 in the right upper limb, 3/5 proximally and 2/5 distally in the right lower limb
Reflexes were brisk bilaterally with right ankle clonus
Noncontrast CT of the head showed no acute pathology
incidental 4 × 6 mm hyperdense focus in the left parasagittal frontal cortex suggestive of a cavernoma
Brain MRI showed a recent ischemic infarction in the left paramedian medulla without hemorrhagic transformation
A diagnosis of ischemic stroke in a 36‐year‐old gentleman with no apparent risk factors was made

concepts.why: The patient presented with acute right-sided weakness and vomiting, and brain MRI showed a recent ischemic infarction in the left paramedian medulla.
Noncontrast CT of the head showed an incidental 4 × 6 mm hyperdense focus in the left parasagittal frontal cortex suggestive of a cavernoma.
The patient was diagnosed with ischemic stroke, but no apparent risk factors were found.
The patient presented with acute right-sided weakness and numbness, and motor strength was 0/5 in the right upper limb and 3/5 proximally and 2/5 distally in the right lower limb.
Brain MRI showed a recent ischemic infarction in the left paramedian medulla.
The patient was a 36-year-old man who presented with ischemic stroke, which is unusual for his age group.

rationales.F01: Acute right-sided weakness and vomiting suggest a stroke, which is more common in older adults, but can occur in young adults.
rationales.F02: Headache and vomiting followed by right-sided numbness and weakness are consistent with a stroke.
rationales.F07: Motor strength deficits are consistent with a stroke, particularly in the right upper and lower limbs.
rationales.F08: Brisk reflexes and ankle clonus are consistent with an upper motor neuron lesion, such as a stroke.
rationales.F10: The presence of a cavernoma could be a potential cause of the stroke, but it is not definitive.
rationales.F11: The recent ischemic infarction in the left paramedian medulla is consistent with a stroke, and the lack of hemorrhagic transformation suggests an ischemic rather than hemorrhagic stroke.
rationales.F12: The diagnosis of ischemic stroke in a young adult with no apparent risk factors suggests that further investigation is needed to determine the cause.
